finding.expected: Preserve the fail-closed access boundary without forbidding the canonical Human-owned challenge path. Rewrite the STOP condition so acquisition stops/remains unauthorized when a challenge would require automated solving, automated retry, bypass, evasion, proxy, stealth, or when no legitimate Human-operated resolution path is available. Explicitly preserve that a Human may resolve a CAPTCHA/security challenge outside ordinary AIOS verification and that any resume remains explicit and separately authorized; challenge resolution itself grants no evidence, collector, test, or action authority. Add or tighten focused governance regression so this distinction cannot regress. Do not modify any production Python, roadmap sequencing, AIOS state, P7/P8 semantic owner, or any other TASK-228 boundary.
finding.issue: Section 7 currently makes acquisition stop or remain unauthorized whenever "the source requires CAPTCHA solving", grouping CAPTCHA solving with evasion, bypass, proxy/stealth, and unsafe access behavior. That is materially inconsistent with the same candidate's Section 8 and the canonical P6 live-capture boundary, where CAPTCHA/security-challenge handling is explicitly Human/operator-owned and ordinary AIOS automation must not solve, retry, bypass, proxy, or evade it. A legitimate later bounded live operation may therefore pause on a challenge, let the Human resolve it outside AIOS verification, and resume only through a fresh explicit authorized operation. The current STOP wording instead prohibits that Human-owned path outright and collapses "manual Human challenge resolution" into "automated/evasive CAPTCHA handling".
